I used to think the public access to the net would result in a beneficial change to society. I was only half right. It has amplified ignorance and reduced discourse to mindless drivel. My first use of a networked computer was in 1979 or 1980. Even then, I thought it would fundamentally change society if everyone had access.

But, I thought that change would be for the better.

Back then, it cost dollars - like four of them, PER MINUTE to connect. Not per hour, per minute. Not adjusted numbers but in 1980 dollars. Well, probably more like 1983 by then. The university paid for it, so I didn't much care. It was like $12/hour when I was in grad school, so the price had dropped. I could also dial into my university by then. I'd taken four years to go back in the military and save some cash up, as I wasn't smart enough to get my doctorate research and education completely funded. So, I skipped from 83 to 87.

By the time I graduated, it was like $6 per hour and still was not open to the public. There were BBSes, chat servers, and things like that. You'd dial into the network you wanted to communicate with. Some services offered larger networks, which were a mix of services. AOL and CompuServe were two big ones.

Then, we had the advent of the WWW. It was still expensive and costs were usually per hour. It was slow and populated mostly by geeks. It was still pretty expensive.

Then, it became a low monthly price to compete with other offerings, and phone companies really got involved, making it even less expensive. It still wasn't too bad, even though you'll sometimes hear me bitch about the day they gave AOL users access to usenet. Eternal September, never forget. Things were moving quickly.

It stayed like that for a while, prices still dropping. Sure, in the turn of the century it was going downhill, but it still was not too bad.

People had to be seated in front of their computer. Broadband wasn't really all that widespread. It was still considered geeky.

Then came the fucking smartphone. It was okay, until they made data cheap. It was not too bad until everyone had a smartphone and the ability to broadcast their fucking idiocy anywhere they could get a signal. The prices dropped and the sizes of data plans increased. Now, they are cheap and ubiquitous.
